name: Cerro Garabitas, Casa de Campo
story: At 677 m, Garabitas is one of the highest points of the Casa de Campo, the former royal hunting estate through which Nationalist columns attacked Madrid in November 1936. Varela's troops took the hill on 13 November and held it for the rest of the war despite Republican counter-attacks, including by the XI International Brigade. From December 1936 their batteries here shelled the city centre, the Gran Vía and the Telefónica building. The front line across the park stayed almost static until March 1939, and several concrete bunkers from both sides still survive in the woods.
see: A panoramic summit with a ranger watchtower and views over Madrid; scattered bunkers and trench traces in the surrounding park.
plan: Free, open park; walk up from the Lago or Batán Metro stations (about 45 minutes). Take a map: signage for war remains is limited.
